avoid_supplements.name: Mineral oil
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Both agents increase fat-soluble vitamin malabsorption and may increase docusate systemic absorption; concurrent use increases risk of lipid pneumonitis if aspirated
avoid_supplements.action: Separate dosing by at least 2 hours; avoid concurrent use in elderly or those with swallowing difficulties

caution_supplements.name: Psyllium husk or other bulk-forming laxatives
caution_supplements.mechanism: Combined laxative effect may enhance bowel activity; generally safe but may cause excessive stooling
caution_supplements.action: Counsel on adequate hydration; monitor for dehydration or electrolyte imbalance with prolonged use

caution_supplements.name: Fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K)
caution_supplements.mechanism: Docusate may slightly increase fecal fat excretion, potentially reducing absorption of fat-soluble vitamins
caution_supplements.action: Monitor vitamin status with chronic docusate use; separate dosing by 2+ hours if possible

caution_foods.name: High-fat foods
caution_foods.mechanism: May increase docusate absorption and GI transit time; excessive dietary fat may worsen stool consistency changes
caution_foods.action: Maintain balanced diet; consistent fat intake recommended during docusate therapy

caution_foods.name: Inadequate fluid intake
caution_foods.mechanism: Docusate efficacy depends on adequate hydration; insufficient water intake reduces stool softening effect
caution_foods.action: Ensure patient consumes at least 6-8 glasses of water daily for optimal therapeutic effect

monitoring_notes: Docusate undergoes minimal systemic absorption and hepatic metabolism, making drug-supplement interactions uncommon. Monitor for dehydration, electrolyte imbalances, and adequate fluid intake during chronic use, particularly in elderly patients or those on concurrent laxatives.
